locations.name: Wray Castle on Windermere
locations.significance: Large medieval-inspired structure built 1840-1847 at cost of £60,000; Potter family stayed July 1882

locations.name: Lingholm Estate
locations.significance: First rented by Potters in summer 1885; location with lively red squirrels that inspired The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin

locations.name: Esthwaite Water
locations.significance: Potter's favorite lake with pastoral landscape and abundant wildlife; inspired Mr. Jeremy Fisher's home

locations.name: Hill Top Farm, Near Sawrey
locations.significance: Potter's first land purchase using book royalties; became her personal space for painting and writing

locations.name: Fawe Park Estate
locations.significance: Less formal estate near Derwentwater with productive kitchen gardens that inspired Mr. McGregor's garden

locations.name: Buckle Yeat cottage
locations.significance: Cottage with splendid flower gardens appropriated as Duchess the Pomeranian's house

locations.name: Lakefield (Ees Wyke), Near Sawrey
locations.significance: Location of Mrs. Lord's cottage whose interior rooms Potter studied for The Pie and the Patty-Pan

locations.name: Newlands Valley
locations.significance: Real inspiration for mountain scenes in The Tale of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle

locations.name: Derwent Bay
locations.significance: Views still recognizable today from The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin, beyond the fells and Walla Crag

locations.name: National Trust properties
locations.significance: Organization to which Potter donated land; maintains Hill Top Farm as Potter left it

trueFalse.statement: Potter purchased Hill Top Farm using royalties as an act of independence from her family.
trueFalse.correction: This first land purchase in the Lake District represented her financial independence.

trueFalse.statement: William Heelis was Potter's publisher before becoming her husband.
trueFalse.correction: William Heelis was her property solicitor, not her publisher. They shared love for Lake District and long walks.

trueFalse.statement: Wray Castle took 7 years to build and cost £60,000.
trueFalse.correction: Built in mock-Norman style, though the owner's wife refused to live there because design was excessively Romantic.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin ends with the squirrel keeping his magnificent tail.
trueFalse.correction: Squirrel Nutkin narrowly escapes death but loses his magnificent tail in the process.

trueFalse.statement: Miss Cameron continued teaching Beatrix Potter art lessons into the 1890s.
trueFalse.correction: Miss Cameron stopped in 1883, just one year after Wray Castle holiday, because Beatrix had surpassed her abilities.

trueFalse.statement: Potter painted squirrels using the same technique as mice, with fine individual hairs.
trueFalse.correction: Potter used layer washes for squirrels with fluid lines to express lively nature, while mice had painstaking fine detail.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Benjamin Bunny was set in Mr. McGregor's garden, inspired by Fawe Park's kitchen gardens.
trueFalse.correction: The abundant kitchen gardens at Fawe Park near Lingholm Estate provided inspiration for the setting.

trueFalse.statement: Norman Warne enthusiastically supported Potter's idea for a frog main character from the start.
trueFalse.correction: When Potter kept pushing the frog idea, Norman said it sounded interesting, though Potter thought he may have been sarcastic.

trueFalse.statement: Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle was inspired by Potter's pet hedgehog and a visit from Lucie Carr.
trueFalse.correction: When Carr family visited, daughter Lucie loved playing with Potter's hedgehog, and Potter later sent Lucie's forgotten gloves back with a poem.

trueFalse.statement: Potter brought a frog in a jar to her publisher's office to prove her color choices were accurate.
trueFalse.correction: When Fruing Warne disputed her color decisions for Mr. Jeremy Fisher, she brought a live frog to his office.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of the Pie and the Patty-Pan features two cats named Ribby and Duchess.
trueFalse.correction: Ribby is a cat, but Duchess is a Pomeranian dog based on Mrs. Rogerson's dogs.

trueFalse.statement: Hill Top Farm was maintained exactly as Potter left it according to her instructions to the National Trust.
trueFalse.correction: Potter left detailed outline requiring rooms and furnishings be kept in present condition, and National Trust kept their promise.

trueFalse.statement: Potter preferred Esthwaite Water because it was larger than Windermere and Coniston Water.
trueFalse.correction: She preferred it for its pastoral landscape, abundant wildlife, and quiet beauty despite being smaller.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin and The Tailor of Gloucester both had intricate plots.
trueFalse.correction: Both finished at end of 1903, so next book she and Norman agreed should have simpler plot like Peter Rabbit.

trueFalse.statement: Potter's onion studies from Benjamin Bunny are now housed at the Victoria and Albert Museum.
trueFalse.correction: These detailed studies of onions are preserved at the Victoria and Albert Museum.

trueFalse.statement: Potter typically sketched and painted her animal subjects from photographs.
trueFalse.correction: Potter typically sketched and painted her animal subjects from real life, as in her studies of a cat sleeping.

trueFalse.statement: The Carr family's daughter Lucie was the inspiration for The Tale of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle.
trueFalse.correction: Lucie loved playing with Potter's pet hedgehog Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle, and once left gloves behind that Potter returned with a poem.

trueFalse.statement: Mr. Jeremy Fisher's home was originally set in a Scottish river but moved to Esthwaite Water in the published version.
trueFalse.correction: He also gained many more crazy mishaps during his day in the published version.

trueFalse.statement: The Tale of Ginger and Pickles was the first Potter story to use Near Sawrey setting.
trueFalse.correction: The Tale of the Pie and the Patty-Pan used Near Sawrey images first; Ginger and Pickles was her next book to use this setting.

trueFalse.statement: Autumnal Landscape from 1909 shows bold, almost impressionistic style.
trueFalse.correction: Bold, saturated autumn hues, fluid washes, and fast brushstrokes are quite modern in this plein air watercolor sketch.

quiz.question: Where did Beatrix Potter get the funds to purchase Hill Top Farm?
quiz.correctAnswer: Her book royalties

quiz.question: What was William Heelis's profession before marrying Beatrix Potter?
quiz.correctAnswer: Property solicitor

quiz.question: What is the National Trust?
options: A non-profit that preserves land, buildings, and cultural sites
quiz.correctAnswer: A non-profit that preserves land, buildings, and cultural sites

quiz.question: Who owned Wray Castle?
options: James Dawson, a surgeon from Liverpool
quiz.correctAnswer: James Dawson, a surgeon from Liverpool

quiz.question: How much did it cost to build Wray Castle?
Why did the owner's wife refuse to live at Wray Castle?
options: It was too far from town
quiz.correctAnswer: The design was excessively Romantic

quiz.question: How long after the 1882 Wray Castle holiday did Miss Cameron continue art lessons with Beatrix?
quiz.correctAnswer: Only one more year

quiz.question: Why was Beatrix's hair cut short in a photograph?
options: It was cut during her severe illness at age 18 or 19
It was the fashion of the time
quiz.correctAnswer: It was cut during her severe illness at age 18 or 19

quiz.question: What building is shown in 'Rain: August in the Lake District' painted in 1898?
quiz.correctAnswer: Lingholm Estate

quiz.question: When did Beatrix Potter begin developing The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin?
options: In letters to Noel and Norah Moore while at Lingholm Estate early 1900s
During her stay at Wray Castle in 1882
quiz.correctAnswer: In letters to Noel and Norah Moore while at Lingholm Estate early 1900s

quiz.question: How does The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin end?
options: The squirrel narrowly escapes death but loses his magnificent tail
The squirrel finds his lost treasure
The squirrel returns home safely with his tail
quiz.correctAnswer: The squirrel narrowly escapes death but loses his magnificent tail

quiz.question: How was Beatrix able to closely observe a live squirrel for The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin?
options: Made the squirrel a house of a soap box and hung it inside a big bird cage
Watched wild squirrels through a window
quiz.correctAnswer: Made the squirrel a house of a soap box and hung it inside a big bird cage

quiz.question: Which earlier books had intricate plots that Potter wanted to move away from?
options: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin and The Tailor of Gloucester
The Tale of Peter Rabbit and Benjamin Bunny
The Tale of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle and Mr. Jeremy Fisher
The Pie and the Patty-Pan and Ginger and Pickles
quiz.correctAnswer: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin and The Tailor of Gloucester

quiz.question: What mediums did Potter use in her depiction of Fawe Park gardens?
options: Pencil, pen-and-ink, sepia ink, and watercolor
quiz.correctAnswer: Pencil, pen-and-ink, sepia ink, and watercolor

quiz.question: Where do the onions play a bigger role in The Tale of Benjamin Bunny?
options: They don't appear in the story
quiz.correctAnswer: In the delicate illustrations

quiz.question: How did Beatrix Potter typically sketch and paint her animal subjects?
quiz.correctAnswer: From real life

quiz.question: What was the inspiration for The Tale of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle?
options: Lucie Carr loved playing with Potter's pet hedgehog and left gloves behind
Potter saw a hedgehog in her garden
quiz.correctAnswer: Lucie Carr loved playing with Potter's pet hedgehog and left gloves behind

quiz.question: Why did Potter prefer Esthwaite Water to larger neighbor lakes?
options: Pastoral landscape, abundant wildlife, quiet beauty
It was closer to her home
quiz.correctAnswer: Pastoral landscape, abundant wildlife, quiet beauty

quiz.question: In what year did Potter write the picture letter featuring Mr. Jeremy Fisher to Eric Moore?
What was Norman Warne's response when Potter kept pushing the frog character idea?
options: He said it sounded interesting, but Potter thought it may have been sarcastic
He suggested using a different animal
quiz.correctAnswer: He said it sounded interesting, but Potter thought it may have been sarcastic

quiz.question: What changed from the original Mr. Jeremy Fisher picture letter to the published version?
options: His home moved from a Scottish river to Esthwaite Water and he has more mishaps
The character became a toad instead
quiz.correctAnswer: His home moved from a Scottish river to Esthwaite Water and he has more mishaps

quiz.question: What did Potter do when Fruing Warne disputed her color decisions for Mr. Jeremy Fisher?
options: She brought a frog in a jar to his office
She refused to work with him
quiz.correctAnswer: She brought a frog in a jar to his office

quiz.question: What story was originally titled 'Something Very Very Nice'?
options: The Tale of the Pie and the Patty-Pan
The Tale of Mr. Jeremy Fisher
quiz.correctAnswer: The Tale of the Pie and the Patty-Pan

quiz.question: Who was Ribby in The Tale of the Pie and the Patty-Pan?
quiz.correctAnswer: A cat

quiz.question: Which dog served as the physical model for Potter's character Duchess?
quiz.correctAnswer: Darkie

quiz.question: What happened to the store in The Tale of Ginger and Pickles?
options: It closes because of money troubles
quiz.correctAnswer: It closes because of money troubles

quiz.question: What did Beatrix Potter like about farm life?
options: Predictability of schedules and routines, straightforwardness, realism
quiz.correctAnswer: Predictability of schedules and routines, straightforwardness, realism

quiz.question: Describe the style of Autumnal Landscape created in 1909.
options: Bold, saturated autumn hues, fluid washes, fast brushstrokes, almost impressionistic
quiz.correctAnswer: Bold, saturated autumn hues, fluid washes, fast brushstrokes, almost impressionistic

options: Added on a wing to make room for herself and the Cannon family
Left it exactly as it was
quiz.correctAnswer: Added on a wing to make room for herself and the Cannon family

quiz.question: What did Potter say about the flowers in her Hill Top Farm gardens?

I grew them all from seed
They were all imported from Scotland
